newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures up on Intertie cutbacks.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures up on Intertie cutbacks.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mostly higher midday following news of scheduled maintenance cutbacks next week on the main transmission lines linking the Northwest to southern California, market sources said Friday.
The stronger tone came despite recent weakness tied to mild weather for much of the western U.S. and weak cash prices, they said.
"If you can't transmit cheaper, more plentiful Northwest power to the Southwest, that might be a reason to bid up Palo," said one dealer.

The 3,800 megawatt (MW) AC segment of the Intertie was scheduled at 2,950 MW between 0800-1600 PDT Monday to Friday next week, while the DC line will be limited to 2,360 over the same period, according to the Bonneville Power Administration.
But he and others cautioned the complex may still break down below support levels given ample spot power supplies and weak cash market prices.
In addition, traders said lower natural gas prices could be bearish for electricity futures.
"If natgas breaks below $2.39 (per million British thermal units) it could be bearish for us," said one trader.
As of 1200 EDT, the NYMEX September Henry Hub natural gas contract was up 0.2 cent at $2.43/mmBtu.
The September Palo Verde (PV) contract was up 61 cents per megawatt hour (MWh) at $30.60 at a high for the day after trading as low as $30.10.
October PV was up 40 cents at $23.75, and November was up 10 cents at $22.60.

Electricity for September delivery at the California-Oregon border (COB) was up two cents at $22.75 per MWh. COB for October was up 30 cents at $22.50, and the November contract was up 30 cents at $23.25.
In the cash market, firm peak deliveries for Saturday and Monday at PV were quoted at $25.00-27.00 a MWh and those at COB $17.00-18.00.
Next week, the southern portion of the Southwest was expected to see above normal temperatures, while Colorado and coastal areas were forecast to see seasonal readings.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average below normal in eastern areas and above normal along the coast.
Most baseload units in the West were said to be operating normally early Friday.
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Palo Verde generating complex in Arizona continued to coast down toward its refueling outage in September.
The unit, in Wintersburg, Ariz., was operating at 83 percent power early Friday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
